# Bagisto API

> REST + GraphQL API reference for Bagisto, the Laravel open-source e-commerce platform. This index lists every documented endpoint; open a page URL for its exact request and response.

- Site: https://api-docs.bagisto.com
- Full documentation (single file): https://api-docs.bagisto.com/llms-full.txt
- Agent skills: `npx skills add bagisto/agent-skills`

## Two API surfaces — Shop vs Admin

This API has two separate surfaces. Pick one and do not mix them:

- **Shop API** (customer-facing: catalog, cart, checkout, customer account). REST base `/api/shop/*`; GraphQL endpoint `POST /api/graphql`. Auth: `X-STOREFRONT-KEY` header on every request, plus a customer or guest-cart `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for authenticated/cart calls. Index entries are grouped under `Shop` section headers (e.g. `## GraphQL API › Shop`, `## REST API › Shop`) and their page URLs contain `/shop/`.
- **Admin API** (back-office: manage orders, catalog, customers, marketing, CMS, settings). REST base `/api/admin/*`; GraphQL endpoint `POST /api/admin/graphql`. Auth: an admin Integration `Authorization: Bearer <id>|<token>` — **no** `X-STOREFRONT-KEY`. Index entries are grouped under `Admin` section headers (e.g. `## GraphQL API › Admin`, `## REST API › Admin`) and their page URLs contain `/admin/`.

**How to tell an entry apart:** look at the section breadcrumb (`› Shop` vs `› Admin`) and the URL path segment (`/shop/` vs `/admin/`). GraphQL field names differ too — shop uses e.g. `products` / `categories`, admin uses e.g. `adminCatalogProducts` / `adminCatalogCategories`.

**REST vs GraphQL** — same data, two transports, NOT interchangeable syntax. REST filters go in the query string (`?category_id=&price=&sort=`); GraphQL uses a JSON `filter:` string plus `sortKey`/`reverse` and cursor pagination.

**Read these two cross-cutting references first — they answer what the per-endpoint pages assume you already know:**
- **Authentication** (https://api-docs.bagisto.com/api/authentication) — which header for which surface; the login `token` (not `apiToken`) is the Bearer for both transports; credential lifetimes; there is **no refresh token** (recover by re-login / regenerate).
- **Identifiers** (https://api-docs.bagisto.com/api/graphql-api/identifiers) — GraphQL exposes both `id` (IRI string) and `_id` (numeric); REST uses the numeric id. Store/compare `_id`, pass `id` back to operations.

- [Test & Ship](/api/for-developers/test-and-ship): An endpoint is not done when it returns data in Postman. It is done when both transports are covered by tests and integrators can discover it.
- [Write Endpoints](/api/for-developers/write-endpoints): A write takes an **input DTO**, runs through a **processor**, and returns a result. The same processor serves the REST `Post` and the GraphQL mutation.

- [Appearance](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance): Appearance is where a store chooses how the storefront looks. It holds two things: the themes the installation has, and the sections each channel draws inside…

## GraphQL API › Admin › Appearance › Sections

- [Sections](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections): A section is one block of a storefront page. Each belongs to one theme and one channel, carries content per locale, and is drawn in the order the channel gives…
- [createAdminAppearanceSection](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/create): Adds a section to a theme and channel. The section is created **switched off with a staged on-state**, so it is drawn in the editor and its preview but not on…
- [deleteAdminAppearanceSection](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/delete): Removes a section and its content for every locale. Media the section uploaded is cleaned up with it.
- [adminAppearanceSection](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/detail): One section with every locale's content.
- [createAdminAppearanceSectionDiscard](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/discard): Throws away every staged edit of a theme and channel. The published content, statuses and order are left exactly as they are, so the storefront does not change.
- [createAdminAppearanceSectionDraft](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/draft): Holds a section's content as an unpublished draft for one locale. The storefront keeps drawing the published content until…
- [createAdminAppearanceSectionDuplicate](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/duplicate): Copies a section, including its content in every locale, into the same theme and channel.
- [adminAppearanceSectionFields](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/fields): The field set a section's type is built from, together with the values it currently holds. This is what makes a client-side editor possible without knowing the…
- [adminAppearanceSections](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/list): The sections a channel holds for a theme, in the order they are drawn, with `footer_links` last. Returns a plain list — one channel's page layout is not…
- [adminAppearanceSectionPreview](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/preview): The sections a channel would draw if its staged edits were published: draft content replaces published content, staged status and order are applied, sections…
- [createAdminAppearanceSectionPublish](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/publish): Promotes every staged edit of a theme and channel — content in all locales, on/off states and order — to what the storefront draws. Sections holding nothing…
- [createAdminAppearanceSectionReorder](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/reorder): Stages the order sections are drawn in. `footer_links` is moved back to the end of whatever order is sent, and the payload returns the order that was actually…
- [createAdminAppearanceSectionStatus](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/status): Stages a section on or off. Like every other edit, it reaches the storefront only when the theme is published.
- [updateAdminAppearanceSection](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/sections/update): Writes a section's **published** values — what the storefront draws immediately. To hold a change back until publishing, use…

## GraphQL API › Admin › Appearance › Themes

- [Themes](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/themes): The theme gallery: every theme the installation knows about, and which channels run each of them.
- [createAdminAppearanceThemeActivate](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/themes/activate): Points one or more channels at a theme. Each channel keeps its own theme, so activating on one leaves the others alone.
- [adminAppearanceTheme](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/themes/detail): One theme by its code.
- [adminAppearanceThemeImpact](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/themes/impact): What activating a theme on the given channels would leave behind. Reports only; nothing is written.
- [adminAppearanceThemes](/api/graphql-api/admin/appearance/themes/list): Every theme the installation knows about, active ones first. Returns a plain list — the gallery is small and not paginated.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Catalog

- [List Products](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products): The canonical admin product listing — a cursor-paginated query mirroring the Catalog → Products datagrid, with every scalar column the listing can resolve.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Catalog › Attributes

- [Attributes](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/attributes): Attributes are the fields a product can carry — `name`, `price`, `color`, `material`, and so on. The Attributes menu lists, creates, edits, and deletes them,…
- [Catalog Attribute Options — Create / Update / Delete (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/attributes/attribute-options): Add a new option to a select/multiselect/checkbox attribute. The parent attribute is named by attributeId in the input. Returns the created option.
- [Catalog Attribute — Create (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/attributes/attributes-create): Create a new product attribute with optional translations and options. Returns the full attribute detail.
- [Catalog Attribute — Delete (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/attributes/attributes-delete): Deletes a user-defined attribute and returns the deleted snapshot. Refused for system attributes and attributes still attached to families.
- [Catalog Attribute — Detail (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/attributes/attributes-detail): Fetch a single attribute by IRI including all locale translations and — for select/multiselect/checkbox types — all options with their own translations.
- [Catalog Attributes — Datagrid Listing (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/attributes/attributes-listing): Cursor-paginated query returning the flat attribute list — the GraphQL equivalent of the admin Catalog → Attributes datagrid. Supports filtering by code, type,…
- [Catalog Attribute — Mass Delete (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/attributes/attributes-mass-delete): Delete a batch of user-defined attributes in one mutation. The whole batch is pre-validated — if any id is a system attribute, nothing is deleted.
- [Catalog Attribute — Update (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/attributes/attributes-update): Update an existing attribute. code is immutable; type cannot change while products reference the attribute. Supplying options replaces the full option set.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Catalog › Categories

- [Categories](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/categories): Categories are the storefront's browsing tree — the sections customers navigate and products are assigned to. The Categories menu lists them (flat or as a…
- [Category — Create (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/categories/categories-create): Create a new category. On create, the translatable fields (slug, name, description) are sent at the top level and broadcast to the configured locales.…
- [Category — Delete (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/categories/categories-delete): Delete a category. Refused for the root category or any category referenced as a channel root. The payload returns a snapshot of the deleted record.
- [Catalog Category — Detail (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/categories/categories-detail): Fetch a single category by ID including the full translations array (all locales present in the DB) and the list of filterable attribute IDs.
- [Catalog Categories — Datagrid Listing (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/categories/categories-listing): Cursor-paginated query returning the flat category list — the GraphQL equivalent of the admin Catalog → Categories datagrid. Supports filtering by name,…
- [Category — Mass Delete (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/categories/categories-mass-delete): Bulk-delete a batch of categories. The whole batch is validated up front — if any id is non-deletable (root or a channel root), nothing is deleted.
- [Category — Mass Update Status (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/categories/categories-mass-update-status): Bulk-set the status (enabled or disabled) on a batch of categories.
- [Catalog Categories — Tree (Nested) (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/categories/categories-tree): Cursor-paginated GraphQL query that returns root category nodes, each carrying its full nested subtree under `children`. Supports locale, status, and rootId…
- [Category — Update (and Move) (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/categories/categories-update): Update a category. Translatable fields are nested under the locale key. Re-parenting and re-positioning (move) are done on this same mutation — there is no…

## GraphQL API › Admin › Catalog › Families

- [Attribute Families](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/families): An attribute family is the **template of fields a product carries**. Every product belongs to exactly one family, and the family decides which attributes (and…
- [Attribute Family — Create (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/families/families-create): Create an attribute family with optional nested groups and per-group custom attributes.
- [Attribute Family — Delete (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/families/families-delete): Delete a family. Refused if it is the default family or any product still uses it.
- [Catalog Attribute Family — Detail (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/families/families-detail): Fetch a single attribute family by IRI including all attribute groups and — within each group — all associated attributes with pivot position. The…
- [Catalog Attribute Families — Datagrid Listing (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/families/families-listing): Cursor-paginated query returning the flat attribute family list — the GraphQL equivalent of the admin Catalog → Attribute Families datagrid. Supports filtering…
- [Attribute Family — Update (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/families/families-update): Update a family, optionally restructuring its attribute groups.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Catalog › Products

- [Products](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products): The full Catalog → Products datagrid. Cursor pagination via first / after. All scalar fields (including special-price) resolve over GraphQL; relation blocks…
- [Catalog Product — Copy](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/copy): Duplicates an existing product across all sub-resources. Refuses configurable variants.
- [Catalog Product — Create](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/create): Step-1 create for a simple product. Only sku, attributeFamilyId and type are submitted; everything else is added later via the Update mutation.
- [Product Customer-Group Prices — Create (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/customer-group-prices-create): Adds a new tier-price row to a product. A null customerGroupId makes the price apply to every group.
- [Product Customer-Group Prices — Delete (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/customer-group-prices-delete): Deletes a single tier-price row and echoes a snapshot of the row as it was just before deletion. Pass the product as productId and the row IRI as input.id.
- [Product Customer-Group Prices — List (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/customer-group-prices-list): Plain list of the tier-price rows attached to a product.
- [Product Customer-Group Prices — Update (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/customer-group-prices-update): Partially updates a tier-price row. Pass only the fields you change.
- [Catalog Product — Delete](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/delete): GraphQL counterpart of DELETE /api/admin/catalog/products/{id}. For configurable products, variants cascade.
- [Product Images — Delete](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/images-delete): Removes the DB row and the file on storage.
- [Product Images — Reorder](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/images-reorder): Update positions of one or more existing images for a product. Each image ID must belong to the product.
- [Product Images — Update](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/images-update): Edit the alt text and the position of an already-uploaded image.
- [Product Images — Upload](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/images-upload): GraphQL upload is NOT supported — binary file parts are not transportable over JSON GraphQL. Use the REST endpoint.
- [Product Inventories — List](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/inventories-list): Cursor connection of per-source inventory rows for a product.
- [Product Inventories — Bulk Update (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/inventories-update): Parent-scoped mutation. Pass a source id with a positive qty to set it, qty 0 to zero it out; sources not in the payload are left untouched. The mutation…
- [Add-Product Search (Create-Order)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/list): The slim product search behind the admin Create-Order "Add Product" modal. Not the product listing — for the full datagrid with every column and filter use…
- [Catalog Products — Mass Delete](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/mass-delete): Deletes a batch of products in one call. Ids that do not exist are skipped without an error, and `deleted` lists only the ones actually removed.
- [Catalog Products — Mass Update Status](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/mass-update-status): GraphQL counterpart of POST /api/admin/catalog/products/mass-update-status. Fires catalog.product.update.{before,after} per ID.
- [Catalog Product — Detail (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/products-detail): Fetch a single catalog product by IRI. Every nested block is a field-selectable Relay connection, so sub-select only what you need. Type-specific connections…
- [Catalog Product — Update](/api/graphql-api/admin/catalog/products/update): Full update of a simple product covering every field on the edit form. Structural/common fields (price, cost, special price, weight, status, categories,…

## GraphQL API › Admin › Cms › Pages

- [CMS Pages](/api/graphql-api/admin/cms/pages): CMS Pages are **static storefront content pages** — About Us, Privacy Policy, custom landing pages, and the like. Each page is served on the storefront at its…

## GraphQL API › Admin › Cms › Pages › Mutations

- [CMS Page — Create](/api/graphql-api/admin/cms/pages/mutations/create): Top-level fields are broadcast to every locale at creation.
- [CMS Page — Delete](/api/graphql-api/admin/cms/pages/mutations/delete): Deletes a CMS page by IRI and returns a snapshot of the removed record.
- [CMS Pages — Mass Delete](/api/graphql-api/admin/cms/pages/mutations/mass-delete): Bulk-delete CMS pages. Non-existent IDs are silently skipped.
- [CMS Page — Update](/api/graphql-api/admin/cms/pages/mutations/update): Validation is LOCALE-NESTED. Top-level `locale` names which block is being updated.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Cms › Pages › Queries

- [CMS Page — Detail](/api/graphql-api/admin/cms/pages/queries/detail): Returns a single CMS page with the full htmlContent body, all translations, and channels. translations and channels are field-selectable connections — query…
- [CMS Pages — List](/api/graphql-api/admin/cms/pages/queries/list): Cursor-paginated CMS pages listing. translations and channels are field-selectable connections — query them via edges { node { … } }.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Configuration

- [Configuration (Admin)](/api/graphql-api/admin/configuration): The admin **Configuration** screen edits Bagisto's store-wide settings — order
- [Configuration Menu (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/configuration/menu): Discover the fields under a slug. include_values is false, so no values are embedded.
- [Configuration Slugs (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/configuration/slugs): Discover every configuration slug (section / group key) you can pass to the Values and Update operations.
- [Configuration Update (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/configuration/update): Bulk-upsert a code → value map under a slug. Returns the re-resolved values.
- [Configuration Values (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/configuration/values): Effective values for every field under sales.order_settings.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Customers

- [Customers](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers): The Customers section is where you manage everyone who shops on the storefront and the records attached to them — their accounts, address books, internal…
- [Customer Active Cart Items (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/active-cart-items): Items in the customer's own active storefront cart (carts.is_active = 1).
- [Customer Addresses (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/addresses): All saved addresses for a customer — billing/shipping picker on the Create-Order screen.
- [Customer Compare Items (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/compare-items): The customer's compare list for the Create-Order sidebar.
- [Create Draft Cart](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/create-draft-cart): Bootstrap an empty admin draft cart for a customer (Create-Order entry).
- [Customer Recent Order Items (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/recent-order-items): Up to 5 most-recent distinct items the customer has ordered.
- [Customer Wishlist Items (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/wishlist-items): The customer's wishlist for the Create-Order sidebar.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Customers › Addresses

- [Delete Customer Address (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/addresses/delete): Removes an address from a customer's address book. `customerId` is **required** and must own the address — omitting it or passing a different customer returns…
- [Customer Address Detail (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/addresses/detail): Fetches a single saved address for a customer by its id. The address must belong to the `customerId` passed in, otherwise an error is returned.
- [Set Customer Address as Default (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/addresses/set-default): Marks the chosen address as the customer's default. All the customer's other addresses have their default flag cleared in the same call.
- [Update Customer Address (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/addresses/update): Updates an existing customer address. Send only the fields you want to change. `customerId` is **required** and must own the address — omitting it or passing a…

## GraphQL API › Admin › Customers › Gdpr

- [GDPR Requests](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/gdpr): The GDPR Requests menu manages the privacy requests customers raise — to **export** their personal data or to **delete** their account. It is the admin's queue…
- [Delete GDPR Request (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/gdpr/delete): The delete response returns a snapshot of the removed request.
- [GDPR Request Detail (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/gdpr/detail): Returns a single GDPR request by IRI, with the requesting customer's name and email resolved inline.
- [Download GDPR Data Export (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/gdpr/download-data): Ad-hoc JSON dump of every table referencing the customer. `data` is a JSON value — query it bare.
- [List GDPR Requests (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/gdpr/list): Cursor pagination over the GDPR data-request queue. Each request has a type (update or delete) and a moderation status.
- [Process GDPR Request (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/gdpr/process): The GraphQL input uses requestId because id is reserved as the resource IRI on mutation inputs.
- [Update GDPR Request (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/gdpr/update): Status + message only. Use the process mutation for the destructive cascade.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Customers › Groups

- [Customer Groups](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/groups): The Customer Groups menu manages the named groups customers are sorted into — such as *general*, *wholesale*, and *guest*. A group is the lever that drives…
- [Create Customer Group (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/groups/create): Creates a new customer group. API-created groups are always user-defined (`isUserDefined: 1`) — the three built-in system groups cannot be created through the…
- [Delete Customer Group (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/groups/delete): Deletes a customer group. On success the deleted record is no longer addressable, so the `adminCustomerGroup` payload comes back `null`.
- [Customer Group Detail (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/groups/detail): Fetches a single customer group by id, including the detail-only `customersCount` (the number of customers currently assigned to the group).
- [List Customer Groups (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/groups/list): User-defined groups whose name matches a term, sorted by code ascending. Filter args, sorting and pagination all combine in one query (multiple filters narrow…
- [Mass Delete Customer Groups (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/groups/mass-delete): Deletes several customer groups in one call. Each id is checked individually — system groups and groups with customers attached are skipped with a reason…
- [Update Customer Group (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/groups/update): Updates a customer group. Send only the fields you want to change.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Customers › Impersonate

- [Impersonate](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/impersonate): The Impersonate menu is the API equivalent of the admin datagrid's **"Login as Customer"** action — it lets an admin act as a customer to reproduce an issue,…
- [Impersonate Customer (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/impersonate/create): Returns a short-lived customer token the admin can use to act as the customer.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Customers › Main

- [Customers](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/main): The Customers menu manages the shopper accounts registered in your store — listing and searching them, viewing a full profile, and creating, editing, deleting,…
- [Create Customer (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/main/create): createAdminCustomer mutation. sendPassword defaults to true and emails the new customer their credentials.
- [Delete Customer (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/main/delete): The delete response returns a snapshot of the removed customer.
- [Customer Detail](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/main/detail): Single customer with the linked group as a nested object and the detail-only counters resolved.
- [List Customers (Datagrid)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/main/list): Cursor pagination. The customer group is a nested object. Detail-only counters are null on the listing.
- [Mass Delete Customers (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/main/mass-delete): Deletes the supplied customer ids in one call. The per-id active-orders guard skips any customer with pending/processing orders, returning the skipped ids with…
- [Mass Update Customer Status (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/main/mass-update-status): Activates or deactivates the supplied customers in one call. `value` must be `0` (inactive) or `1` (active).
- [Update Customer (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/customers/main/update): Partial update — send only the fields you change.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Customers › Notes

## GraphQL API › Admin › Marketing › Promotions

- [Promotions](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions): Promotions are the store's **discounting engine**. There are two kinds, and they fire at different moments in the shopping journey.
- [Create Cart Rule Coupon](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rule-coupons-create): Add a single coupon code to a cart rule.
- [Delete Cart Rule Coupon](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rule-coupons-delete): Delete a coupon by id. A successful delete returns no errors; the coupon is removed.
- [Generate Cart Rule Coupons](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rule-coupons-generate): Bulk-create several coupon codes from a format, prefix and suffix.
- [List Cart Rule Coupons](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rule-coupons-list): Cursor-paginated list of every coupon belonging to one cart rule.
- [Mass Delete Cart Rule Coupons](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rule-coupons-mass-delete): Delete several coupons of one cart rule in a single call. Ids not on the rule are skipped.
- [Copy Cart Rule](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rules-copy): Duplicate an existing cart rule into a brand-new, inactive rule. The new rule copies channels and customer groups but not coupons.
- [Create Cart Rule](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rules-create): Create a coupon-gated cart rule that discounts the cart by a percentage for a channel and customer group.
- [Delete Cart Rule](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rules-delete): Delete a cart rule by id. A successful delete returns no errors; the rule is removed.
- [Cart Rule Detail](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rules-detail): Full payload for a single cart rule, including conditions, channels, and customer groups.
- [List Cart Rules](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rules-list): Cursor-paginated list of every cart rule.
- [Mass Delete Cart Rules](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rules-mass-delete): Delete several cart rules in one call. Non-existent ids are silently skipped.
- [Update Cart Rule](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rules-update): Update a cart rule's name and discount. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change.
- [Create Catalog Rule](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-create): Create a catalog rule that reduces price by a percentage for a channel and customer group.
- [Delete Catalog Rule](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-delete): Delete a catalog rule by id. The mutation returns a snapshot of the just-deleted rule plus a success message.
- [Catalog Rule Detail](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-detail): Full payload for a single catalog rule, including conditions, channels, and customer groups.
- [List Catalog Rules](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-list): Cursor-paginated list of every catalog rule.
- [Mass Delete Catalog Rules](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-mass-delete): Delete several catalog rules in one call. Non-existent ids are silently skipped.
- [Update Catalog Rule](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-update): Update a catalog rule's name and discount. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Marketing › Search Seo

- [Search & SEO](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo): Search & SEO controls **how the store is searched and how search engines index it**. It mirrors the admin **Marketing → Search & SEO** menu.
- [Create Search Synonym](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-create): Create a synonym group so a search for any term also matches the others.
- [Delete Search Synonym](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-delete): Delete a search synonym group by id. A successful delete returns no errors; the group is removed.
- [Search Synonym Detail](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-detail): Full payload for a single search synonym group.
- [List Search Synonyms](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-list): Cursor-paginated list of every search synonym group.
- [Mass Delete Search Synonyms](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-mass-delete): Delete several search synonym groups in one call. Non-existent ids are silently skipped.
- [Update Search Synonym](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-update): Update a synonym group's terms. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change.
- [Delete Search Term](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-terms-delete): Delete a search term by id. A successful delete returns no errors; the term is removed.
- [Search Term Detail](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-terms-detail): Full payload for a single search term.
- [List Search Terms](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-terms-list): Cursor-paginated list of every recorded search term.
- [Mass Delete Search Terms](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-terms-mass-delete): Delete several search terms in one call. Non-existent ids are silently skipped.
- [Update Search Term](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-terms-update): Update a search term's phrase and optional redirect URL. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change.
- [Create Sitemap](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-create): Create a sitemap definition. Creating the row does not build the XML files — call generate afterwards.
- [Delete Sitemap](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-delete): Delete a sitemap by id. A successful delete returns no errors; the row and its generated XML files are removed.
- [Sitemap Detail](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-detail): Full payload for a single sitemap, including the generated index file and per-batch sitemap paths.
- [Generate Sitemap](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-generate): Build the actual XML files for a sitemap, once per channel it covers, and record the written paths.
- [List Sitemaps](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-list): Cursor-paginated list of every sitemap definition.
- [Update Sitemap](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-update): Update a sitemap's file name. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change. It does not regenerate the XML.
- [Create URL Rewrite](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-create): Create a 301 redirect from an old path to a target path for a CMS page.
- [Delete URL Rewrite](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-delete): Delete a URL rewrite by id. A successful delete returns no errors; the rewrite is removed.
- [URL Rewrite Detail](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-detail): Full payload for a single URL rewrite.
- [List URL Rewrites](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-list): Cursor-paginated list of every URL rewrite.
- [Mass Delete URL Rewrites](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-mass-delete): Delete several URL rewrites in one call. Non-existent ids are silently skipped.
- [Update URL Rewrite](/api/graphql-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-update): Update a URL rewrite's target path and redirect type. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Reporting

- [Reporting](/api/graphql-api/admin/reporting): The Reporting menu returns the deep, dedicated reports behind the admin **Reporting** screens — **Sales**, **Customers** and **Products** — plus an API-only…
- [Reporting — Customers (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/reporting/customers): New-customer registrations in the window, compared against the previous period, plus an over-time series (previous vs. current) for the chart line.
- [Reporting — Overview (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/reporting/overview): Total revenue for the period (default `type`). Carries a previous-vs-current comparison plus a per-day `over_time` series for charting.
- [Reporting — Products (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/reporting/products): Default report. Total units sold in the window vs. the previous window, plus a per-day `over_time` series for the chart line.
- [Reporting — Sales (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/reporting/sales): Gross sales for the window vs. the previous period, plus an over-time series split into previous and current buckets. This is the default type.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Sales › Carts

- [Add Item to Cart](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/add-item): Add a simple/virtual product. `id` is the resource IRI; `cartId` is forwarded as the raw integer for the processor.
- [Apply a Coupon](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/apply-coupon): Apply a cart-rule coupon code to the draft cart. Returns errors[] on unknown/inactive coupon (404 equivalent) or already-applied (422 equivalent).
- [Get Cart](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/get-cart): Read a draft cart by IRI. `id` is the resource IRI `/api/admin/carts/{cartId}`.
- [List Payment Methods](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/list-payment-methods): List payment methods supported for the draft cart. A shipping method must be selected first.
- [List Shipping Methods](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/list-shipping-methods): Returns available shipping rates for a draft cart. Both addresses must be saved first.
- [Place Order](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/place-order): Finalise a fully prepared draft cart into a real order.
- [Remove Applied Coupon](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/remove-coupon): Remove the currently-applied coupon from the draft cart. Idempotent.
- [Remove a Cart Item](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/remove-item): Remove a single line item from the draft cart.
- [Save Cart Addresses](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/save-address): Save billing (and optionally shipping) addresses on the draft cart.
- [Set Payment Method](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/set-payment-method): Save the chosen payment method on the draft cart.
- [Set Shipping Method](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/set-shipping-method): Save the chosen shipping method on the draft cart.
- [Update Cart Item Quantities](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/carts/update-items): Bulk-update line-item quantities. `qty` is a map of cartItemId → new quantity.

- [Refund Preview](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/orders/refund-preview): Compute refund totals (subtotal, discount, tax, shipping, grandTotal) without saving anything.
- [Reorder](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/orders/reorder): Build a fresh admin draft cart from a previous order's items. Returns the new cart ID.
- [Send Duplicate Invoice](/api/graphql-api/admin/sales/orders/send-duplicate-invoice): Emails a copy of the invoice. The recipient is the email you pass, or the order's customer email when omitted.

- [List Channels](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/channels/list): List every channel (storefront) configured in the store, with cursor pagination.
- [Update Channel](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/channels/update): Partially update a channel. Omitted fields are left unchanged; omitting the locale / currency / inventory-source arrays preserves the existing assignments.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Settings › Data Transfer Imports

- [Index Import (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports): Runs the final indexing stage. The field name follows API Platform naming — clients typically alias it. Runs against an import that has finished linking.
- [Cancel Import (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports/cancel): Aborts a pending or processing import. The field name follows API Platform naming — clients typically alias it.
- [Create Import (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports/create): Creating an import requires a multipart file upload, which GraphQL cannot carry. The mutation rejects with an error directing you to the REST endpoint.
- [Delete Import (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports/delete): Removes an import job and its uploaded source file. Returns a snapshot of the deleted record so you can confirm exactly which import was removed.
- [Import Detail (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports/detail): Returns a single import job with the full set of fields — including the heavy `errors[]` list and `summary` object that the listing leaves null.
- [Link Import (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports/link): Runs the post-process linking stage. The field name follows API Platform naming — clients typically alias it. Runs against an import that has finished…
- [List Imports (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports/list): Narrow by entity type, action and state, then sort by created_at descending. Filter args, sorting and pagination all combine in one query. Supplying multiple…
- [Data Transfer Imports](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports/overview): The Data Transfer Imports menu bulk-imports records into the store from a CSV / XLSX / XML file — products, customers, tax rates, and any other entity your…
- [Start Import (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports/start): Processes the next pending batch of rows. The field name follows API Platform naming — clients typically alias it. Runs against a validated import.
- [Import Stats (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports/stats): Returns the current progress of an import **without advancing it**. Poll this between [start](./start.md) / [link](./link.md) / [index](./index.md) calls to…
- [Validate Import (GraphQL)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/data-transfer-imports/validate): Runs the validation pass over the uploaded file. The field name follows API Platform naming — clients typically alias it.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Settings › Exchange Rates

- [Exchange Rates](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/exchange-rates): The Exchange Rates menu defines the conversion rate from your store's **base currency** to each other currency you allow. When a shopper views the storefront…
- [Create Exchange Rate](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/exchange-rates/create): Create a new exchange rate for a target currency that does not yet have one.
- [Delete Exchange Rate](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/exchange-rates/delete): Delete a single exchange rate by its IRI. The deleted record is returned in the response.
- [Exchange Rate Detail](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/exchange-rates/detail): Fetch a single exchange rate by its IRI.
- [List Exchange Rates](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/exchange-rates/list): Cursor-paginated list of every exchange rate, each with its target currency code/name and rate.
- [Mass Delete Exchange Rates](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/exchange-rates/mass-delete): Delete several exchange rates at once by their numeric ids.
- [Update Exchange Rate](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/exchange-rates/update): Change the rate of an existing exchange rate. The target currency stays fixed.
- [Update Rates (auto-sync)](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/exchange-rates/update-rates): Refresh every target currency's rate from the store's configured external rate provider. Takes an empty input.

- [List Inventory Sources](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/inventory-sources/list): Cursor-paginated list of inventory sources. Every column is populated on each row.

- [Update Inventory Source](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/inventory-sources/update): Partial update — send the id plus only the fields you want to change. Returns the full source.

## GraphQL API › Admin › Settings › Return Custom Fields › Mutations

- [Delete RMA custom field](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/return-custom-fields/mutations/delete): Deletes a RMA custom field. Pass the resource IRI as `id`. Permission: `sales.rma.custom-fields.delete`.
- [Mass Delete RMA custom fields](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/return-custom-fields/mutations/mass-delete): Deletes several RMA custom fields in one call. Permission: `sales.rma.custom-fields.delete`.

- [Update a Tax Category](/api/graphql-api/admin/settings/tax-categories/update): Update a tax category's details and re-sync its attached tax rates. The taxrates list you send fully replaces the current set.

- [Revoke a GDPR Request](/api/graphql-api/shop/gdpr-requests/mutations/revoke-gdpr-request): Withdraw a pending or processing GDPR data request owned by the authenticated customer.

- [List GDPR Requests](/api/graphql-api/shop/gdpr-requests/queries/list-gdpr-requests): Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated customer's own GDPR data requests, newest first.
- [View GDPR Request](/api/graphql-api/shop/gdpr-requests/queries/view-gdpr-request): Retrieve a single GDPR data request owned by the authenticated customer.

## GraphQL API › Shop › Locales

- [Locales](/api/graphql-api/shop/locales): The Locales menu exposes the languages the storefront is published in. A client uses it to discover which locales are available — and the details of each one…

## GraphQL API › Shop › Locales › Queries

- [Get Locales](/api/graphql-api/shop/locales/queries/locales): Retrieve all store locales with basic information.
- [Get Single Locale](/api/graphql-api/shop/locales/queries/single-locale): Retrieve a single locale by ID with basic information.

## GraphQL API › Shop › Mutations

- [Add to Cart](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/add-to-cart): Add a simple product to the cart. Simple products only require `productId` and `quantity` — no additional options are needed.
- [Apply Coupon](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/apply-coupon): Apply a valid coupon code to reduce cart total.
- [Cancel Customer Order](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/cancel-customer-order): Cancel a customer order that is in pending status, restoring inventory to stock.
- [Create Cart](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/create-cart): Create a new shopping cart session.
- [Create Compare Item](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/create-compare-item): Add a product to the authenticated customer's comparison list. The customer is auto-detected from the Bearer token.
- [Create Contact Us](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/create-contact-us): Send a contact-form enquiry. Public — the storefront key is the only credential needed, and a customer token is not used.
- [Create Customer Address](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/create-customer-address): Create a new address for the authenticated customer.
- [Create Newsletter](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/create-newsletter): Subscribe an email address to the newsletter on the current channel. A customer token is optional and only links the subscription to that account.
- [Create Product Review](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/create-product-review): Create a basic product review with title, comment, and rating.
- [Create Wishlist Item](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/create-wishlist): Add a product to the authenticated customer's wishlist.
- [Customer Login](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/customer-login): Authenticate a customer with email and password.
- [Customer Logout](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/customer-logout): Logout a customer and invalidate their authentication tokens.
- [Customer Registration](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/customer-registration): Register a new customer account with email and password.
- [Verify Customer Token](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/customer-verify-token): Verify a customer's email using a verification token.
- [Delete All Compare Items](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/delete-all-compare-items): Remove all compare items for the authenticated customer. Returns the count of deleted items.
- [Delete All Wishlist Items](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/delete-all-wishlists): Remove all wishlist items for the authenticated customer. Returns the count of deleted items.
- [Delete Compare Item](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/delete-compare-item): Remove a product from the customer's comparison list by its IRI.
- [Delete Customer Address](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/delete-customer-address): Delete a customer address.
- [Delete Customer Account](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/delete-customer-profile): Permanently delete the authenticated customer's account.
- [Delete Product Review](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/delete-product-review): Delete a product review by providing its ID in IRI format.
- [Delete Wishlist Item](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/delete-wishlist): Delete a specific wishlist item by its IRI.
- [Forgot Password](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/forgot-password): Request a password reset email for an account.
- [Merge Cart](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/merge-cart): Merge a guest cart into the authenticated customer's cart. Pass the guest cart's _id as cartId and the customer's Bearer token in the Authorization header.…
- [Move Wishlist Item to Cart](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/move-wishlist-to-cart): Move a wishlist item to the shopping cart and remove it from the wishlist.
- [Place Order](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/place-order): Cash-on-delivery or money-transfer — the order is created immediately.
- [Remove Cart Item](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/remove-cart-item): Remove a specific item from the shopping cart.
- [Remove Coupon](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/remove-coupon): Remove an applied coupon code from the cart.
- [Reorder Customer Order](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/reorder-customer-order): Add all items from a previous order to the customer's cart.
- [Set Checkout Address](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/set-billing-address): Set the billing address and use it as the shipping address too by setting useForShipping to true.
- [Set Payment Method](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/set-payment-method): Set the payment method for a cart.
- [Set Shipping Method](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/set-shipping-method): Set the shipping method for a checkout.
- [Social Login](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/social-login): Sign in (or sign up) with a Google ID token from Google Identity Services (web) or the Google SDK (mobile).
- [Toggle Wishlist Item](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/toggle-wishlist): Toggle a product in the wishlist. If the product is not in the wishlist, it gets added.
- [Update Cart Item](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/update-cart-item): Modify the quantity of an item in the shopping cart.
- [Update Customer Address](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/update-customer-address): Update an existing customer address.
- [Update Customer Profile](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/update-customer-profile): Update the authenticated customer's profile information.
- [Update Product Review](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/update-product-review): Update basic product review information like title and comment.
- [Upload Customizable File](/api/graphql-api/shop/mutations/upload-customizable-file): A file-type customizable option needs a binary upload, which cannot travel over GraphQL. Upload the file over REST to get a token, then reference the token in…

## GraphQL API › Shop › Queries

- [Categories](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/categories): Retrieve categories with pagination using first and after arguments.
- [Download Downloadable Product](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/download-downloadable-product): Download the actual purchased downloadable product file. Requires customer authentication. Each download decrements the remaining download count.
- [Download Invoice](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/download-invoice): Download a customer invoice as PDF using the downloadUrl with Bearer token authentication.
- [Get Checkout Addresses](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-addresses): Retrieve the address applied to the current checkout session — either the guest-entered address or the authenticated customer's selected checkout address.
- [Get Attribute](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-attribute): Retrieve basic attribute information by ID.
- [Get Attribute Options](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-attribute-options): Retrieve basic attribute options with pagination.
- [Get Attributes](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-attributes): Retrieve a paginated list of all product attributes with basic information.
- [Get Booking Slots](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-booking-slots): |
- [Get Cart](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-cart): Retrieve the current shopping cart with all items.
- [Get Category](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-category): Retrieve basic information for a single category by its ID.
- [Get Category Attribute Filters](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-category-attribute-filters): Fetch the filters available on a category, with the price range for the slider.
- [Get Channel](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-channel): Retrieve basic information for a single channel by its ID.
- [Get Channels](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-channels): Retrieve all store channels with basic information.
- [Get Compare Item](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-compare-item): Retrieve a specific compare item by its IRI.
- [Get Compare Items](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-compare-items): Retrieve paginated compare items for the authenticated customer using cursor-based pagination.
- [Get Countries](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-countries): Retrieve all available countries with basic information.
- [Get Country](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-country): Retrieve basic information for a single country by its ID.
- [Get Country State](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-country-state): Retrieve a single state by ID with basic information.
- [Get Country States](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-country-states): Retrieve all states for a specific country with basic information.
- [Get Currencies](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-currencies): Retrieve all store currencies with basic information.
- [Get Single Currency](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-currency): Retrieve a single currency by ID with basic information.
- [Get Customer Addresses](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-addresses): Retrieve all saved addresses for the authenticated customer with cursor-based pagination.
- [Get Customer Downloadable Product](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-downloadable-product): Retrieve details of a specific downloadable product purchase by its IRI identifier.
- [Get Customer Downloadable Products](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-downloadable-products): Retrieve a paginated list of downloadable product purchases for the authenticated customer using cursor-based pagination.
- [Get Customer Invoice](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-invoice): Retrieve details of a specific invoice by its IRI identifier.
- [Get Customer Invoices](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-invoices): Retrieve the invoice for a specific order with detailed invoice line items. Each order has exactly one invoice.
- [Get Customer Order](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-order): Retrieve details of a specific customer order by its IRI identifier.
- [Get Customer Order Shipment](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-order-shipment): Retrieve details of a specific shipment by its ID with tracking information and line items.
- [Get Customer Order Shipments](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-order-shipments): Retrieve all shipments for a specific customer order with tracking details and line items.
- [Get Customer Orders](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-orders): Retrieve a paginated list of orders for the authenticated customer using cursor-based pagination.
- [Get Customer Profile](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-profile): Retrieve the authenticated customer's profile information.
- [Get Customer Review](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-review): Retrieve a specific product review by ID for the authenticated customer.
- [Get Customer Reviews](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-customer-reviews): Retrieve all product reviews submitted by the authenticated customer with pagination.
- [Single CMS Page](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-page): Retrieve a single CMS page by its ID, including the resolved-locale translation and every stored translation.
- [CMS Pages](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-pages): Retrieve all CMS pages with their translation details using cursor-based pagination.
- [Get Payment Methods](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-payment-methods): Retrieve available payment methods for checkout.
- [Single Product](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-product): Retrieve a single product by its ID. `isInWishlist` / `isInCompare` need the customer Bearer token and are `"0"` for guests.
- [Product Reviews](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-product-reviews): Retrieve product reviews with basic fields and pagination.
- [Get Products](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-products): For a signed-in customer, every product carries 'isInWishlist' and 'isInCompare' fields.
- [Get Shipping Methods](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-shipping-methods): Retrieve available shipping methods for checkout.
- [Get Wishlist Item](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-wishlist): Retrieve a specific wishlist item by its IRI.
- [Get Wishlists](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/get-wishlists): Retrieve paginated wishlist items for the authenticated customer using cursor-based pagination.
- [Search Products](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/search-products): Search products by query term with sorting and filtering options.
- [Tree Categories](/api/graphql-api/shop/queries/tree-categories): Retrieve root and child categories with their basic hierarchical structure.

## GraphQL API › Shop › Returns

- [Returns (RMA)](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns): Returns — also called RMA (Return Merchandise Authorization) — let a logged-in customer ask the store to take back or cancel an item they ordered. A customer…

## GraphQL API › Shop › Returns › Mutations

- [Cancel a Return](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/mutations/cancel-return): Cancel the authenticated customer's own return (RMA) request.
- [Close a Return](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/mutations/close-return): Mark the authenticated customer's own return (RMA) request as solved.
- [Raise a Return](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/mutations/create-return): Raise a new return (RMA) request for one item of one of the authenticated customer's orders.
- [Reopen a Return](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/mutations/reopen-return): Reopen a canceled or declined return (RMA) request back to pending.
- [Send a Return Message](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/mutations/send-return-message): Add a customer message to the conversation thread of a return (RMA) request.

## GraphQL API › Shop › Returns › Queries

- [List Return Custom Fields](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/queries/list-return-custom-fields): List the active custom fields the storefront return form asks the shopper to fill in.
- [List Return Messages](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/queries/list-return-messages): List the conversation messages of a return (RMA) request owned by the authenticated customer, newest first.
- [List Return Reasons](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/queries/list-return-reasons): List the active reasons a customer can pick when raising a return, filtered by resolution type.
- [List Returnable Items](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/queries/list-returnable-items): List the return-eligible items of one of the authenticated customer's orders, with the quantity caps the store enforces.
- [List Returnable Orders](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/queries/list-returnable-orders): The customer's orders a return can still be raised against — the list the New Request flow opens with.
- [List Returns](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/queries/list-returns): Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated customer's own return (RMA) requests, newest first.
- [View Return](/api/graphql-api/shop/returns/queries/view-return): Retrieve a single return (RMA) request owned by the authenticated customer, including its item, images and action flags.

## REST API › Admin › Appearance › Sections

- [Sections](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections): A section is one block of a storefront page. Each belongs to one theme and one channel, carries content per locale, and is drawn in the order the channel gives…
- [Create Section](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/create): Adds a section to a theme and channel. The section is created **switched off with a staged on-state**, so it is drawn in the editor and its preview but not on…
- [Delete Section](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/delete): Removes a section and its content for every locale. Media the section uploaded is cleaned up with it.
- [Get Section](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/detail): One section with every locale's content.
- [Discard](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/discard): Throws away every staged edit of a theme and channel. The published content, statuses and order are left exactly as they are, so the storefront does not change.
- [Stage Edits](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/draft): Holds a section's content as an unpublished draft for one locale. The storefront keeps drawing the published content until…
- [Copy Section](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/duplicate): Copies a section, including its content in every locale, into the same theme and channel.
- [Section Fields](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/fields): The field set a section's type is built from, together with the values it currently holds. This is what makes a client-side editor possible without knowing the…
- [List Sections](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/list): The sections a channel holds for a theme, in the order they are drawn, with `footer_links` last. Returns a plain array — the set is one channel's page layout,…
- [Upload Media](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/media): Stores one image or video against a section and returns the path to record in its options. This endpoint is REST only — a binary upload cannot be carried over…
- [Preview](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/preview): The sections a channel would draw if its staged edits were published: draft content replaces published content, staged status and order are applied, sections…
- [Publish](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/publish): Promotes every staged edit of a theme and channel — content in all locales, on/off states and order — to what the storefront draws. Sections holding nothing…
- [Stage Order](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/reorder): Stages the order sections are drawn in. `footer_links` is moved back to the end of whatever order is sent, and the response returns the order that was actually…
- [Stage Status](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/status): Stages a section on or off. Like every other edit, it reaches the storefront only when the theme is published.
- [Update Section](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/sections/update): Writes a section's **published** values — what the storefront draws immediately. To hold a change back until publishing, use [Stage…

## REST API › Admin › Appearance › Themes

- [Themes](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/themes): The theme gallery: every theme the installation knows about, and which channels run each of them.
- [Activate Theme](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/themes/activate): Points one or more channels at a theme. Each channel keeps its own theme, so activating on one channel leaves the others alone.

- [List Themes](/api/rest-api/admin/appearance/themes/list): Every theme the installation knows about, active ones first. Not paginated — the gallery is small and returned whole.

## REST API › Admin › Catalog › Categories

- [Catalog Category — Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/categories/categories-detail): Single category record including the full translations array (all locales present in the DB) and the list of filterable attribute IDs.

- [Category — Mass Update Status](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/categories/categories-mass-update-status): Sets the status of a batch of categories to the given value (0 or 1).

## REST API › Admin › Catalog › Families

- [Attribute Families](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/families): An attribute family is the **template of fields a product carries**. Every product belongs to exactly one family, and the family decides which attributes (and…
- [Attribute Family — Create](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/families/families-create): Creates an attribute family with optional nested attribute groups and per-group `custom_attributes`. `code` must be unique and pass the Code rule.
- [Attribute Family — Delete](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/families/families-delete): Refuses with HTTP 400 if the family is the last one in the store, or if any product is still using it.
- [Catalog Attribute Family — Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/families/families-detail): Single attribute family record including all attribute groups and — within each group — all associated attributes with their pivot position. Use this to…
- [Catalog Attribute Families — Datagrid Listing](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/families/families-listing): Paginated, filterable, sortable attribute family list mirroring the Bagisto admin Catalog → Attribute Families datagrid. Returns the standard `{ data, meta }`…
- [Attribute Family — Update](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/families/families-update): Update a family. Inside `attribute_groups`, items keyed by numeric id update existing groups; items keyed by `group_*` create new groups; omitted existing ids…

## REST API › Admin › Catalog › Products

- [Products](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products): The full Catalog → Products datagrid. Paginated { data, meta } envelope. Heavy relation blocks and a few EAV-derived fields are null on the listing…

- [Catalog Product — Create (step 1)](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/create): Step-1 create for a simple product. Only sku, attribute_family_id and type are submitted; everything else (name, price, inventory, images) is added later via…
- [Product Customer-Group Prices — Create](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/customer-group-prices-create): Creates a new tier-price row. `customer_group_id: null` makes the price apply to every customer group. The combination `(qty, customer_group_id)` must be…
- [Product Customer-Group Prices — Delete](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/customer-group-prices-delete): Deletes a single customer-group price row.
- [Product Customer-Group Prices — List](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/customer-group-prices-list): Lists every customer-group price row attached to the product, in the standard admin `{ data, meta }` envelope.
- [Product Customer-Group Prices — Update](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/customer-group-prices-update): Partially updates the given tier-price row. The new `(qty, customer_group_id)` combination must remain unique for the product.
- [Catalog Product — Delete](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/delete): Deletes a catalog product. For configurable products, all variants cascade. No "refuse if in non-completed order" guard — mirrors Bagisto admin behaviour.
- [Downloadable Products — Download File](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/downloadable-download): Streams the stored file for a product attribute (a downloadable product's file/sample attribute) as a binary attachment.
- [Downloadable Products — Upload Link / Sample File](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/downloadable-upload): Multipart upload of the binary file for a file-type downloadable link. Returns the stored path to use on the product update.
- [Export Products](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/export): Download the products datagrid as a CSV file — the same data the admin Catalog → Products "Export" button produces. Honours the same filters as the listing and…
- [Product Images — Delete](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/images-delete): Deletes the DB row and removes the file from public storage.
- [Product Images — Reorder](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/images-reorder): Updates the position of one or more existing images for a product. Each image ID must belong to the product or the request is rejected.
- [Product Images — Update](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/images-update): Edit the alt text and the position of an already-uploaded image.
- [Product Images — Upload](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/images-upload): Multipart upload of a single product image. Allowed mime types — bmp, jpeg, jpg, png, webp.
- [Product Inventories — List](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/inventories-list): Returns one row per inventory_source that has a product_inventories entry for the product. The envelope `meta.totalQty` is the sum across all sources.
- [Product Inventories — Bulk Update](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/inventories-update): Mirrors Bagisto monolith `ProductController::updateInventories`. Sources passed with qty=0 are kept but zeroed-out; sources NOT in the payload are left…
- [Add-Product Search (Create-Order)](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/list): The slim product search behind the admin Create-Order "Add Product" modal. Not the product listing — for the full datagrid with every column and filter use…
- [Catalog Products — Mass Delete](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/mass-delete): Deletes a batch of catalog products in one call. Ids that do not exist are skipped without an error, and `deleted` lists only the ones actually removed.
- [Catalog Products — Mass Update Status](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/mass-update-status): Bulk-flips the `status` flag of a batch of products to either 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled). Mirrors Bagisto monolith `ProductController::massUpdate` —…
- [Catalog Product — Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/products-detail): Single catalog product record with all detail-level fields populated. Type-specific blocks (superAttributes/variants for configurable, bundleOptions for…
- [Catalog Product — Update](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/update): Partial update — send only the attribute codes you change. Every attribute on the product's family is editable by its code (name, url_key, price, status,…
- [Product Videos — Delete](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/videos-delete): Removes the video's DB row and its file from public storage.
- [Product Videos — Upload](/api/rest-api/admin/catalog/products/videos-upload): Multipart upload of a single product video. Allowed types — mp4, webm, ogg, mov.

## REST API › Admin › Customers

- [Customers](/api/rest-api/admin/customers): The Customers section is where you manage everyone who shops on the storefront and the records attached to them — their accounts, address books, internal…
- [Customer Active Cart Items](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/active-cart-items): Items in the customer's OWN active storefront cart (carts.is_active = 1) — the right-sidebar "Cart Items" panel on the Create-Order screen.
- [Customer Addresses](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/addresses): All saved addresses for a customer — used by the Create-Order screen's billing / shipping picker.
- [Customer Compare Items](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/compare-items): The customer's compare list — the right-sidebar "Compare Items" panel on the Create-Order screen.

- [Customer Recent Order Items](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/recent-order-items): Up to 5 most-recent distinct items the customer has ordered. Right-sidebar panel on the Create-Order screen.
- [Customer Wishlist Items](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/wishlist-items): The customer's wishlist — the right-sidebar "Wishlist Items" panel on the Create-Order screen.

- [Delete Customer Address](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/addresses/delete): Removes an address from a customer's address book. Returns a confirmation message.
- [Customer Address Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/addresses/detail): Returns a single saved address for a customer.
- [Set Customer Address as Default](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/addresses/set-default): Sets the chosen address as the customer's default and clears the default flag on all their other addresses. Empty body.
- [Update Customer Address](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/addresses/update): Edits an existing customer address. The update is partial — send only the fields you want to change. The response is the full updated address detail.

- [Process GDPR Request](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/gdpr/process): Approves a pending request AND, for `type=delete`, cascades the customer deletion.

## REST API › Admin › Customers › Groups

- [Customer Groups](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/groups): The Customer Groups menu manages the named groups customers are sorted into — such as *general*, *wholesale*, and *guest*. A group is the lever that drives…

- [Delete Customer Group](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/groups/delete): Removes a customer group. Returns a confirmation message.
- [Customer Group Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/groups/detail): Returns a single customer group, including the `customersCount` that the listing omits.
- [List Customer Groups](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/groups/list): Lists the customer groups customers can be segmented into, returned in the `{ data, meta }` envelope.
- [Mass Delete Customer Groups](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/groups/mass-delete): Deletes several customer groups in one request. The response reports which ids were `deleted` and which were `skipped` (with a reason).
- [Update Customer Group](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/groups/update): Edits a customer group. The update is partial — send only the fields you want to change. The response is the updated group.

## REST API › Admin › Customers › Main

- [Customers](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/main): The Customers menu manages the shopper accounts registered in your store — listing and searching them, viewing a full profile, and creating, editing, deleting,…
- [Create Customer](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/main/create): Creates a new customer and returns the full customer record. When `send_password` is true (default) a random password is generated and the credentials are…
- [Delete Customer](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/main/delete): Refuses with HTTP 400 if the customer has any pending/processing orders.
- [Customer Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/main/detail): Returns the full customer record with the group as a nested object plus the detail-only counters (`totalAddresses`, `totalOrders`, `totalAmountSpent`).
- [List Customers (Datagrid)](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/main/list): DataGrid-parity listing. Each row carries the customer's group as a nested object. Detail-only counters are not part of listing rows.
- [Mass Delete Customers](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/main/mass-delete): Customers with active orders are skipped with a reason instead of aborting the batch.
- [Mass Update Customer Status](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/main/mass-update-status): Sets `status` on every supplied customer. `value` must be `0` or `1`.
- [Update Customer](/api/rest-api/admin/customers/main/update): Partial update. Email uniqueness excludes self. Returns the full customer record (group nested under `group`).

## REST API › Admin › Marketing › Promotions

- [Promotions](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions): Promotions are the store's **discounting engine**. There are two kinds, and they fire at different moments in the shopping journey.
- [Create Cart Rule Coupon](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rule-coupons-create): Add a single coupon code to a cart rule.

- [Copy Cart Rule](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rules-copy): Duplicate an existing cart rule into a brand-new, inactive rule. Coupons are not copied.

- [Mass Delete Cart Rules](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rules-mass-delete): Delete several cart rules in one call. Non-existent ids are silently skipped.
- [Update Cart Rule](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions/cart-rules-update): Update a cart rule's name and discount. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change.
- [Create Catalog Rule](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-create): Create a catalog rule that reduces price by a percentage for a channel and customer group.
- [Delete Catalog Rule](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-delete): Delete a catalog rule by id.
- [Catalog Rule Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-detail): Full payload for a single catalog rule, including conditions, channels, and customer groups.
- [List Catalog Rules](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-list): Paginated list of every catalog rule, returned in the { data, meta } envelope.
- [Mass Delete Catalog Rules](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-mass-delete): Delete several catalog rules in one call. Non-existent ids are silently skipped.
- [Update Catalog Rule](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/promotions/catalog-rules-update): Update a catalog rule's name and discount. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change.

## REST API › Admin › Marketing › Search Seo

- [Search & SEO](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo): Search & SEO controls **how the store is searched and how search engines index it**. It mirrors the admin **Marketing → Search & SEO** menu.
- [Create Search Synonym](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-create): Create a synonym group so a search for any term also matches the others.
- [Delete Search Synonym](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-delete): Delete a search-synonym group by id.
- [Search Synonym Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-detail): Full payload for a single search-synonym group.
- [List Search Synonyms](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-list): Paginated list of every search-synonym group, returned in the { data, meta } envelope.
- [Mass Delete Search Synonyms](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-mass-delete): Delete several synonym groups in one call. Non-existent ids are silently skipped.
- [Update Search Synonym](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-synonyms-update): Update a synonym group's terms. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change.
- [Delete Search Term](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-terms-delete): Delete a search term by id.
- [Search Term Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-terms-detail): Full payload for a single search term, including its result count and use count.
- [List Search Terms](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-terms-list): Paginated list of every recorded search term, returned in the { data, meta } envelope.
- [Mass Delete Search Terms](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-terms-mass-delete): Delete several search terms in one call. Non-existent ids are silently skipped.
- [Update Search Term](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/search-terms-update): Update the term text and optional redirect URL. Counts are storefront-recorded and not editable.
- [Create Sitemap](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-create): Create a sitemap definition. The XML is not built on save — call generate explicitly.
- [Delete Sitemap](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-delete): Delete a sitemap by id. Removes the row and its generated XML files.
- [Sitemap Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-detail): Full payload for a single sitemap, including the built index file and child sitemap paths.
- [Generate Sitemap](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-generate): Build the XML files for a sitemap. Send an empty body — the id comes from the URL.
- [List Sitemaps](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-list): Paginated list of every sitemap definition, returned in the { data, meta } envelope.
- [Update Sitemap](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/sitemaps-update): Update a sitemap's file name. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change.
- [Create URL Rewrite](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-create): Create a 301 redirect from an old CMS page path to a new target path.
- [Delete URL Rewrite](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-delete): Delete a URL rewrite by id.
- [URL Rewrite Detail](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-detail): Full payload for a single URL rewrite.
- [List URL Rewrites](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-list): Paginated list of every URL rewrite, returned in the { data, meta } envelope.
- [Mass Delete URL Rewrites](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-mass-delete): Delete several URL rewrites in one call. Non-existent ids are silently skipped.
- [Update URL Rewrite](/api/rest-api/admin/marketing/search-seo/url-rewrites-update): Change the target path and redirect type. Update is a partial merge — send only the fields you change.
